title: Pulse_Secure_VPN_Compromise_Investigation_213
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise involving the PULSECHECK malware family.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity potentially related to the PULSECHECK malware family, a known threat that establishes persistent access and enables lateral movement within compromised networks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise. The PULSECHECK malware is particularly dangerous as it can lead to data breaches, unauthorized access, and significant operational disruptions.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is at IP address 192.168.50.5. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is at IP address 192.168.50.5. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you've noticed unusual outbound connections from the target system on port 4444. Investigate these connections to determine if they're malicious.
levels.solution: Check active network connections and listen ports on the target system. The suspicious port number is 4444. The flag type is a port number.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the nature of network connections and how they can be investigated.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for commands that can display active network connections and listening ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to check active network connections and listen ports.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Service
levels.content: You've identified a suspicious service named `bkd.service` running on the target system. Analyze this service to understand its behavior and determine if it's related to the PULSECHECK malware.
levels.solution: Examine the service configuration files and process details. The service name is `bkd.service`. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand what service configuration files and process details can tell you about a service.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for commands that can display the status and details of a service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bkd.service` to check the status of the suspicious service.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Evidence suggests that the attacker may be moving laterally within the network using a service named `payload-transfer.service`. Investigate the target system to find evidence of lateral movement.
levels.solution: Check for file transfers and remote execution commands. The service name is `payload-transfer.service`. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand what file transfers and remote execution commands can indicate about lateral movement.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for commands that can display the status and details of a service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status payload-transfer.service` to check the status of the suspicious service.
